# Tela

> Tela is a desktop UI framework in pure Go (no cgo, no webview): React-style components and hooks, styled with Tailwind CSS v4 classes, drawn by its own renderer on Linux and Windows, and rendered headlessly to PNGs and aria snapshots so an agent can see what it built. This file is the whole guide an LLM needs to build good-looking Tela screens: the API, the `kit` components (shadcn/ui's look), the agent loop with `tela mcp`, a complete settings screen and the mistakes to avoid. Every Go block in it compiles against the current API.

Contents: 1 Start · 2 The agent loop · 3 Elements and props · 4 Components and hooks · 5 Styling · 6 kit · 7 A complete settings screen · 8 Windows and desktop services · 9 Pitfalls and limits · 10 Testing · More

## 1. Start

- Tela draws every pixel (like Flutter or a browser). There is no HTML, DOM, CSS file or JavaScript: a tree of Go values describes the UI.
- Elements and props come from package `h` (dot-imported, so markup reads like JSX); the app, hooks, events and colors from `tela`; ready-made styled components from `kit`.
- Components are struct values with a `Build() tela.Node` method, or functions wrapped in `tela.C`/`tela.CP`. Hooks (`tela.UseState`...) follow React's rules.
- Styling is `Class("...")` with Tailwind v4 class names, verbatim. Theme tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`) follow light and dark.
- Go 1.27+, always `CGO_ENABLED=0`. Lucide icons are a separate module.

```sh
mkdir myapp && cd myapp && go mod init example.com/myapp
go get github.com/kuronosu/tela@latest github.com/kuronosu/tela/icons/lucide@latest
CGO_ENABLED=0 go install github.com/kuronosu/tela/cmd/tela@latest   # the CLI: tela mcp, snapshot, inspect, lint, dev, run, build
# or: tela new myapp  (a counter app with a test, go.mod ready)
go mod tidy   # after you add imports: kit and aria need golang.org/x/text
```

The imports of a screen:

```go
import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/icons/lucide" // lucide.Check, lucide.Settings, ... (Lucide's file names in CamelCase)
)
```

The smallest complete app. `var App` is the window that `main` opens and the screen that `tela snapshot` and `tela mcp` render:

```go
package main

import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"
)

// Counter is the public name; tela.C gives counter its own hook state.
func Counter() tela.Node { return tela.C(counter) }

func counter() tela.Node {
	count, setCount := tela.UseState(0)
	return Div(Class("flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center"),
		kit.Card{
			Class:       "w-72",
			Title:       Text("Counter"),
			Description: Textf("Clicked %d times", count),
			Footer: kit.Button{Class: "w-full", Children: Text("Add one"),
				OnClick: func() { setCount.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) }},
		})
}

var theme = kit.Theme() // shadcn/ui's neutral colors and 10 px radius: use it with kit

var App = tela.App{
	Title: "Counter", Width: 480, Height: 320,
	Theme: &theme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	Root: Counter(),
}

func main() { tela.Main(App) }
```

**What the CLI and `tela mcp` mount** (the package may be `main` or any package):

- `var Previews = tela.Previews{...}`: several named screens; `--preview NAME` (or the `open` tool) picks one, else the first name in byte order. Wins over the others.
- `func Preview() tela.Node`: one screen, mounted as `tela.C(Preview)`, so it may call hooks itself.
- Otherwise `var App = tela.App{...}`: its `Root` is the screen.
- In every case `var App` (a `tela.App` or `*tela.App`) gives the window: `Width`/`Height` (default 960x640), `RootClass`, `Theme`, `ColorScheme`, `ClassAliases`. Without `RootClass` the window is white with black text.
- `tela.Preview{Root, Wrap}` is one named screen: `Root` is any `tela.Component`; `Wrap func(tela.Node) tela.Node` (optional, no hooks) puts it inside the providers of the contexts it reads. A preview has no size, scheme or state of its own: the size is `App` or `--size`, the scheme `--dark` (the CLI), and the **initial state** comes from fields of a struct component (below).
- Leave `App.ColorScheme` as `tela.System` (the zero value): an explicit `tela.Light` or `tela.Dark` wins over the OS and over `--dark`, so every render would have that scheme.

```go
// One screen; it may use hooks because it is mounted as tela.C(Preview).
func Preview() tela.Node {
	open, setOpen := tela.UseState(true)
	return Div(Class("p-8"), kit.Switch{Checked: &open, OnCheckedChange: setOpen.Set, AriaLabel: "Open"})
}

// Several screens, each started in the state its fields give it.
var Previews = tela.Previews{
	"1 Empty": {Root: Inbox{}},
	"2 Full":  {Root: Inbox{Unread: 12}},
	"3 Open":  {Root: kit.Toaster{Children: Inbox{Unread: 3, Open: true}}},
}

// Unread and Open only choose the first state: the component owns it.
type Inbox struct {
	Unread int
	Open   bool
}

func (in Inbox) Build() tela.Node {
	open, setOpen := tela.UseState(in.Open)
	return Div(Class("p-8 text-sm"), Textf("%d unread", in.Unread),
		kit.Switch{Checked: &open, OnCheckedChange: setOpen.Set, AriaLabel: "Open"})
}
```

**State previews.** `tela snapshot` renders one frame, so to see an edited form, an error or a dialog, make a preview whose struct component has a field that chooses the initial `UseState` (`Start string`, `Scenario string`: the initial form value, which section is open), and give each state its own name in `Previews`. Name the screens `"1 Sign in"`, `"2 Invalid"`... so the first sorts first. To see below the fold, render taller: `tela snapshot --size 1100x1700 --preview "2 Invalid"`.

`tela.App` fields: `Title`, `AppID`, `Width`, `Height`, `RootClass`, `Root` (a `tela.Component`: `Settings()`, `Settings{}`, `kit.Toaster{Children: ...}`), `ColorScheme` (`tela.System`, the zero value, follows the OS; `tela.Light`, `tela.Dark`), `Theme *tela.Theme`, `ClassAliases`, `ClassicScrollbars`, `InstantScroll`, `Dev *bool`. `tela.Main(app)` opens the window and runs until it closes; `tela.Run(app)` returns the error instead.

## 2. The agent loop

Write the package, look at it, fix, repeat. `tela mcp` keeps a headless instance of the screen running and rebuilds it when the source changes.

```sh
claude mcp add tela -- tela mcp ./myapp          # Claude Code; other clients: {"command": "tela", "args": ["mcp", "./myapp"]}
tela mcp [--size WxH] [--scale N] [--dark] [--preview NAME] [pkg]
```

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `snapshot {}` | Aria snapshot (Playwright YAML) with `[ref=eN]` on what you can act on. Cheap: call it after every edit |
| `screenshot {}` / `{"ref": "e5"}` | PNG of the window or one element. Judge the look here: spacing, alignment, contrast, dark mode |
| `click {"ref": "e5"}` | Real pointer click; `"button": "right"`, `"double": true`, or `"x"`, `"y"` |
| `fill {"ref": "e7", "text": "ana@example.com"}` | Replace a text field's value; `"submit": true` presses Enter |
| `press {"key": "Tab"}` | Key or combo in Playwright syntax (`Enter`, `Shift+Tab`, `Control+a`, `ArrowDown`), optionally on a `ref` |
| `hover`, `scroll {"ref", "dy": 400}`, `drag {"from", "to" or "dx"/"dy"}` | Pointer moves, wheel, drags |
| `resize {"width": 390, "height": 844}` / `{"scale": 2}` | Keeps the state; breakpoints follow |
| `open {"dark": true}` / `{"preview": "2 Full"}` | Mount afresh (state reset) in dark mode, another preview, size or scale; `{}` lists the previews |
| `wait {"ms": 500}` / `{"text": "Saved"}` | Advance the app clock (timers, `UseTimeout`, animations, toasts) or wait for a text |
| `inspect {"ref": "e5"}` | Layout JSON: rects, margin/border/padding, classes, class errors, computed style. Use it when something is misplaced |
| `lint {}` | `tela lint -json` on the package |

Elements are named by `ref` (from the latest snapshot), or `role` + `name`, `text`, `testId`, with `nth`. Every acting tool returns the new snapshot.

**Reading a result.** The text has sections: `### Snapshot` (YAML), `### Dev errors` (unknown classes with "did you mean": fix these first), `### Dev warnings` (missing keys, nil dependencies), `### Lint`, `### Output of the app`. A dev-mode panic (an unknown role, a misused hook) is the error of the call, with the fix in its message, and the screen is mounted afresh. A first line "The source changed: rebuilt ... and mounted afresh (state reset)" means your edit is live. "The package does not compile:" is followed by the compiler's errors, and the previous build keeps answering. "The new build compiles, but its screen cannot be mounted" is a panic while mounting (often a hook misuse; the message names the fix).

**A good loop.** 1) Write the screen with `var App` (or `Preview`). 2) `snapshot`: fix every dev error and lint finding. 3) `screenshot`: fix the look. 4) `open {"dark": true}` + `screenshot`. 5) `click`/`fill` the main interactions and `screenshot` the states (open dialogs, toasts after `wait`). 6) `resize` to a narrow window if it must be responsive.

**CLI equivalents** (same rendering, deterministic, no system fonts):

```sh
tela snapshot --size 1040x800 --scale 2 --dark -o out.png ./myapp   # PNG (W*scale x H*scale)
tela inspect ./myapp            # aria snapshot YAML; --layout for the layout JSON
tela lint ./...                 # unknown classes, roles, aria tokens, keys, hook misuse, a prop where a node goes; file:line:col: rule: message
tela lint -fix ./...            # also removes redundant single-child Fragment(x) wrappers
tela dev ./myapp                # a real window that reloads on save, keeping state
tela run ./myapp [args]         # build and run the program (go run); on macOS as a development .app in the user cache
tela build -o dist ./myapp      # the program; GOOS=darwin writes dist/<Name>.app (AppID from App or -id, -name)
```

`tela snapshot` renders one frame: state set by effects, timers or toasts does not show in it; use `tela mcp` (`wait`) or a test for those.

## 3. Elements and props (`h`)

An element takes props and children in one list, in any order: `Div(Class("p-4"), H2(Text("Title")), OnClick(f))`. A string is not a child: `Div("x")` does not compile; write `Div(Text("x"))` or `Textf("%d items", n)`.

**Elements:** `Div` (block box; the general container), `Span` (inline in text; a flex item inside `flex`), `P`, `H1`..`H6` (unstyled, like Tailwind's Preflight: size them with classes; they give heading roles), `Button` (no look of its own, focusable, Enter/Space click), `A` (`Href`; does not navigate: handle `OnClick`), `Strong`, `Em`, `Code`, `Img` (`SrcPath`, `SrcFS`, `SrcBytes`, `Src(image.Image)`, `Alt`; PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG), `Icon(icon, props...)` (an SVG `tela.Icon`, 1em, colored by the text color), `Input`, `Textarea`, `Form` (`OnSubmit`; Enter submits), `Label` (`For`), `Text`, `Textf`, `TextFn(func() string)`, `Fragment(children...)` (no box), `Portal(children...)` (a layer above the window: overlays), `Presence(children...)` (keeps exiting children mounted), `VirtualList`. There is no `Ul`, `Li`, `Nav`, `Section`, `Header`, `Table` or `Select` element: use `Div` with `Role("list")`, `Role("navigation")`... and `kit` components.

**Props:** `Class(classes...)`, `Style(tela.Width(w), tela.Bg(c), ...)` (typed values computed in code; they win over classes), `Key(id)`, `ID`, `For`, `Disabled(bool)`, `TabIndex`, `AutoFocus`, `Ref(elementRef)`, `TestID`, `Dir("rtl")`, `Scheme(tela.Dark)` (a subtree in another color scheme), `Inert`, `Href`, `Alt`, `Tint(color)`; text fields: `Value`, `DefaultValue`, `Bind(text, setText)`, `BindValue(*tela.Value[string])`, `Placeholder`, `Type("email")`, `Rows`, `ReadOnly`, `MaxLength`, `Name`; accessibility: `Role("navigation")`, `AriaLabel`, `AriaLabelledBy(refs...)`, `AriaDescribedBy(ref)`, `AriaCurrent("page")` (`""` is none), `AriaChecked`, `AriaPressed`, `AriaExpanded`, `AriaSelected`, `AriaDisabled`, `AriaInvalid`, `AriaHidden`, `AriaSort`, `AriaRowCount`, `AriaRowIndex`, `AriaHasPopup`, `AriaControls`, `AriaValueNow`, `AriaValueMin`, `AriaValueMax`, `AriaValueText` (live regions are `Role("status")` and `Role("alert")`); animation: `AnimateLayout()`, `LayoutID(id)`, `Exit(classes)`.

**Events:** `OnClick`, `OnDoubleClick`, `OnContextMenu`, `OnMouseDown/Up/Move/Enter/Leave`, `OnPointer...`, `OnLongPress`, `OnDrag`/`OnDragStart`/`OnDragEnd` (the drag gesture), `OnDragEnter`/`OnDragOver`/`OnDragLeave`/`OnDrop` with `Draggable(true)` (HTML's drag and drop, section 8), `OnWheel`, `OnScroll`, `OnKeyDown`/`OnKeyUp`, `OnFocus`/`OnBlur`, `OnChange` (every edit), `OnBeforeInput`, `OnSubmit`, `OnSelect`. Each takes a `func()` or a `func(e)` of its event type (`tela.MouseEvent`, `tela.KeyboardEvent`, `tela.ChangeEvent`...). Events bubble; `e.StopPropagation()`, `e.PreventDefault()`, or wrap a `func()` in `tela.StopPropagation(f)`.

**Helpers:** `If(cond, child)` and `IfElse(cond, a, b)` take and return a `tela.Child` (a node, a struct component or a prop); a `tela.Child` can be returned where a `tela.Node` is expected, and the branch that is off is `nil`, the empty node (a hole that keeps the positions of its siblings; test it with `n == nil`); `Map(items, func(T) tela.Node)` and `MapIndex` (give each node a `Key`); `MapKeyed(items, keyFn, func(T) tela.Node)` keys the nodes for you; `Range(n, func(int) tela.Node)` for static repeats (keyed by index); `Nodes([]tela.Node)` passes a slice built in a loop. Every argument of `If` is evaluated: `If(u != nil, Text(u.Name))` panics on nil `u`; use a Go `if`.

```go
type Todo struct {
	ID   int
	Text string
	Done bool
}

func TodoList(todos []Todo, remove func(id int)) tela.Node {
	return Div(Role("list"), AriaLabel("Todos"), Class("flex flex-col gap-2"),
		If(len(todos) == 0, P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text("Nothing to do."))),
		Map(todos, func(t Todo) tela.Node {
			return Div(Key(t.ID), Role("listitem"),
				Class("flex items-center justify-between rounded-md border border-border px-3 py-2"),
				Span(Class("text-sm"), If(t.Done, Class("text-muted-foreground line-through")), Text(t.Text)),
				Button(Class("text-sm text-destructive hover:underline"), AriaLabel("Remove "+t.Text),
					OnClick(func() { remove(t.ID) }), Text("Remove")))
		}))
}

func Shortcuts(save func()) tela.Node {
	return Div(TabIndex(0), Class("rounded-md p-4 outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"),
		OnKeyDown(func(e tela.KeyboardEvent) {
			if e.CmdOrCtrl() && e.Key == "s" { // Cmd on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere
				e.PreventDefault()
				save()
			}
		}),
		Text("Press Ctrl+S to save"))
}
```

**Raw text fields** (prefer `kit.Input` and `kit.Field`, which are styled and wired):

```go
func Search() tela.Node {
	q, setQ := tela.UseState("")
	return Form(OnSubmit(func() { fmt.Println("search", q) }),
		Input(Type("search"), Placeholder("Search"), AriaLabel("Search"), Bind(q, setQ),
			Class("h-9 w-64 rounded-md border border-input bg-transparent px-3 text-sm placeholder:text-muted-foreground",
				"focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50")))
}
```

**Long lists:** `VirtualList(count, estimateSize, renderItem, props...)` builds only the visible rows; it is the scroll container (style it like a `Div`). `renderItem` returns a `tela.Node` (a struct component is one) and must not call hooks (return a struct component for rows with state). `ItemKey(func(i int) K)` keys rows by identity.

```go
type Row struct{ Name string }

func (r Row) Build() tela.Node {
	return Div(Class("flex h-12 items-center border-b border-border px-4 text-sm"), Text(r.Name))
}

func People(names []string) tela.Node {
	return VirtualList(len(names), func(int) float32 { return 48 },
		func(i int) tela.Node { return Row{Name: names[i]} },
		ItemKey(func(i int) string { return names[i] }),
		Class("h-96 rounded-lg border border-border"))
}
```

## 4. Components and hooks

**Struct components** are the default: the fields are the props, `Build` has a value receiver, children are a field of type `tela.Component` (the same type as `tela.Node`; several via `Fragment(...)`). A struct component is a `tela.Node`, so it can be returned from any function or `Build`, passed to `If`, `Map`, `tela.C` and `Root`, and used as a child, with no wrapper. A struct value used as a child is its own component, with its own state, and its build is skipped while its fields are `==` to the previous ones (func or slice fields make it rebuild every time; that is fine).

```go
type Stat struct {
	Label, Value, Trend string
}

func (s Stat) Build() tela.Node {
	return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-1 rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-5 shadow-xs"),
		P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text(s.Label)),
		P(Class("text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight tabular-nums"), Text(s.Value)),
		P(Class("text-xs font-medium text-emerald-600 dark:text-emerald-400"), Text(s.Trend)))
}

type Section struct {
	Title    string
	Children tela.Component
}

func (s Section) Build() tela.Node {
	open, setOpen := tela.UseState(true)
	return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-3"),
		Button(Class("text-left text-sm font-semibold"), OnClick(tela.Toggle(setOpen)), AriaExpanded(open), Text(s.Title)),
		If(open, s.Children))
}

// A struct component is a tela.Node: return it as it is.
// Never call Section{...}.Build(): its hooks would run in the caller.
func Overview() tela.Node {
	return Section{Title: "This week", Children: Div(Class("grid grid-cols-3 gap-4"),
		Stat{Label: "Revenue", Value: "$12,480", Trend: "+8.1%"},
		Stat{Label: "Orders", Value: "342", Trend: "+3.4%"},
		Stat{Label: "Refunds", Value: "4", Trend: "-1.2%"})}
}
```

**Function components** use `tela.C(fn)` (no props) or `tela.CP(fn, props)` (comparable props, skipped while `==`). Write the wrap once in a public function, so callers never call the private one:

```go
func Clock() tela.Node { return tela.C(clock) }

func clock() tela.Node {
	now, setNow := tela.UseState(time.Now())
	tela.UseInterval(time.Second, func() { setNow.Set(time.Now()) })
	return Span(Class("tabular-nums"), Text(now.Format("15:04:05")))
}

type BadgeProps struct{ Count int }

func Unread(p BadgeProps) tela.Node { return tela.CP(unread, p) }

func unread(p BadgeProps) tela.Node {
	return Span(Class("rounded-full bg-primary px-2 text-xs font-medium text-primary-foreground"), Textf("%d", p.Count))
}
```

Keys: an element takes `Key(id)`; a component or fragment is keyed with `tela.WithKey(Card{...}, id)`, or `tela.C(fn, Key(id))`, `tela.CP(fn, p, Key(id))`, or `MapKeyed`.

**Hooks** (call them at the top of a component, same order every build, never in `if`/`for`/after an early `return`/inside callbacks or `Map` functions):

| Hook | Does |
|---|---|
| `v, set := tela.UseState(init)` | State; `set.Set(v)`, `set.Update(func(T) T)` (use `Update` when the new value depends on the old). `set` is a comparable `tela.Setter[T]`, safe from any goroutine; `tela.Toggle(set)` flips a bool |
| `s, d := tela.UseReducer(reduce, init)` | `d.Dispatch(action)`; reducer `func(S, A) S` |
| `tela.UseEffect(f, deps...)` | After the frame is presented; `f` returns a cleanup or nil. No deps: every build; `tela.Once`: mount only. `UseEffect(f, nil)` panics in dev mode |
| `tela.UseMount(f)`, `tela.UseEffectDo(f, deps...)`, `tela.UseUpdateEffect(f, deps...)` | Mount/unmount; an effect without cleanup; skip the first build |
| `tela.UseLayoutEffect(f, deps...)` | After layout, before paint: measure, scroll into view (the frame is painted scrolled) |
| `tela.UseMemo(compute, deps...)`, `tela.UseOnce(init)` | Cached value; computed once |
| `tela.UseCallback(fn)` | A stable comparable `tela.Callback[F]`; call `cb.Fn()`. Keeps props comparable |
| `r := tela.UseRef(init)` | `r.Current` persists, no rebuild |
| `el := tela.UseElementRef()` + `Ref(el)` | `el.Focus()`, `Blur`, `Click`, `Bounds()`, `ScrollTo/ScrollBy`, `ScrollIntoView()`, `ScrollToIndex(i, tela.AlignEnd)`, `Value()`, `Select()` |
| `tela.UseID()` | A stable unique id (label `For` + input `ID`) |
| `ctx := tela.CreateContext(def)` (package level), `ctx.Provider(v, children...)`, `tela.UseContext(ctx)` | Context; only readers rebuild |
| `v := tela.UseValue(init)` | Observable value: `v.Get()` in build rebuilds; read in a `...Fn` style prop (`tela.WidthFn`, `HeightFn`, `TranslateFn`, `OpacityFn`, `BgFn`, `TextColorFn`) or `TextFn` it only relayouts/repaints. `v.Set` from any goroutine |
| `tela.UseInterval(d, f)`, `tela.UseTimeout(d, f, deps...)` | On the frame clock, no goroutine. `d <= 0` pauses/cancels; a new `d` or deps restarts the timeout |
| `tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context), deps...)` | Background goroutine, cancelled when deps change or on unmount; update the UI through setters |
| `tela.UseSpring(target, opts...)`, `tela.UseTween(target, opts...)` | A `*tela.Value[T]` that animates toward `target` (float32, Color, Point, Size, Rect); feed it to a `...Fn` prop |
| `tela.UsePresence()`, `tela.UsePresenceTween()` | A component's own exit animation inside `h.Presence` |
| `tela.UseColorScheme()`, `tela.UseTheme()`, `tela.UseDirection()`, `tela.UseReducedMotion()` | Environment; `tela.SetColorScheme(tela.Dark)` switches the app |
| `kit.UseToast()`, `kit.UseStyle()` | `kit.ToastHandle` (under a `kit.Toaster`); the active kit recipe |

A custom hook is a function named `UseXxx`/`useXxx` that calls hooks. `tela.Post(f)` runs `f` on the UI thread from any goroutine.

```go
type action struct {
	kind string
	text string
}

func reduce(items []string, a action) []string {
	switch a.kind {
	case "add":
		return append(append([]string(nil), items...), a.text)
	case "clear":
		return nil
	}
	return items
}

var Mode = tela.CreateContext("light")

func DarkNotes() tela.Node { return Mode.Provider("dark", Notes()) }

func Notes() tela.Node { return tela.C(notes) }

func notes() tela.Node {
	items, dispatch := tela.UseReducer(reduce, []string{"Buy milk"})
	draft, setDraft := tela.UseState("")
	last := tela.UseElementRef()
	tela.UseLayoutEffect(func() func() {
		last.ScrollIntoView() // the frame that shows a new note shows it in view
		return nil
	}, len(items))
	mode := tela.UseContext(Mode)
	return Div(Class("flex h-80 flex-col gap-3 p-4"),
		P(Class("text-xs text-muted-foreground"), Textf("Mode: %s", mode)),
		Div(Class("flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1 overflow-y-auto"),
			MapIndex(items, func(i int, s string) tela.Node {
				return P(Key(i), If(i == len(items)-1, Ref(last)), Class("text-sm"), Text(s))
			})),
		kit.Input{Placeholder: "New note", AriaLabel: "New note", Value: &draft, OnValueChange: setDraft.Set},
		kit.Button{Disabled: draft == "", Children: Text("Add"), OnClick: func() {
			dispatch.Dispatch(action{kind: "add", text: draft})
			setDraft.Set("")
		}})
}
```

Smooth values without rebuilds:

```go
func Drawer(open bool) tela.Node {
	target := float32(-320)
	if open {
		target = 0
	}
	x := tela.UseSpring(target) // starts at the target, then springs to new targets
	return Div(Class("fixed inset-y-0 left-0 w-80 border-r border-border bg-background p-6 shadow-xl"),
		Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (float32, float32) { return x.Get(), 0 })), // repaints only
		Text("Menu"))
}

func Download() tela.Node {
	progress := tela.UseValue(float32(0))
	tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context) {
		for i := 1; i <= 10 && ctx.Err() == nil; i++ {
			time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
			progress.Set(float32(i) / 10)
		}
	}, tela.Once)
	return Div(Class("h-2 w-64 overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted"),
		Div(Class("h-full bg-primary"), Style(tela.WidthFn(func() float32 { return 256 * progress.Get() }))))
}
```

## 5. Styling

Classes are Tailwind CSS v4's, verbatim, parsed into typed styles. If you would write it in React + Tailwind v4, write the same here. Order: element defaults, then classes in order (a later class wins over an earlier one that sets the same property; `Class` may repeat and takes several strings), then `Style(...)` props. No cascade, no selectors, no stylesheet. Everything is `border-box`. `Div` is `display: block`, like HTML.

**Supported:** spacing (`p-4`, `px-6`, `m-auto`, `gap-3`, `space-y-4`), sizing (`w-64`, `w-full`, `max-w-3xl`, `min-h-screen`, `size-8`, `h-[72px]`, `aspect-video`), flex (`flex`, `flex-col`, `items-center`, `justify-between`, `flex-1`, `shrink-0`, `grow`, `basis-1/3`, `flex-wrap`, `order-*`), grid (`grid grid-cols-3`, `grid-cols-[200px_1fr]`, `col-span-2`, `auto-rows-*`, `place-items-center`), positioning (`relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky top-0`, `inset-0`, `z-10`), overflow and scrolling (`overflow-y-auto`, `overscroll-contain`, `scroll-smooth`), colors with opacity (`bg-white/15`, `text-zinc-500`, `bg-[#1e1e2e]`), borders (`border`, `border-b`, `border-border`, `rounded-xl`, `rounded-t-lg`, `divide-y divide-border` for the lines between the children, `divide-x-2`, `divide-y-reverse`, `divide-dashed`), `ring-*`, `ring-offset-*`, `outline-*`, shadows (`shadow-sm`...`shadow-2xl`, `shadow-xs`, `inset-shadow-*`), gradients (`bg-linear-to-br from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500`, `bg-radial`, `bg-conic`), typography (`text-sm`, `font-semibold`, `tracking-tight`, `leading-6`, `truncate`, `line-clamp-2`, `text-balance`, `tabular-nums`, `uppercase`, `font-mono`, `font-['Family']`, `whitespace-pre`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `break-words`), effects (`opacity-50`, `blur-sm`, `backdrop-blur`, `drop-shadow-*`, `mix-blend-*`, masks), transforms (`translate-x-2`, `scale-95`, `rotate-45`, `origin-*`; 2D only), transitions (`transition`, `transition-colors`, `duration-200`, `ease-out`, `delay-*`), `animate-spin`/`pulse`/`ping`/`bounce` (also `animate-[bounce_1s_150ms_infinite]`), `cursor-pointer`, `pointer-events-none`, `select-none`, `sr-only`, `field-sizing-content`, background images (`bg-[url(img/hero.jpg)] bg-cover`, files registered with `tela.Assets(fsys)`), `[clip-path:circle(50%)]`, arbitrary values (`w-[calc(50%-8px)]`, `top-[3px]`, `grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr))]`; the theme's variables work inside them: `bg-[conic-gradient(var(--color-primary)_72%,transparent_0)]`, `shadow-[0_0_0_2px_var(--color-ring)]`, `rounded-[var(--radius)]`, `w-[calc(var(--spacing)*4)]`, `bg-(--color-primary)`, with a token's light and dark value following the scheme). Units: `px`, `rem`, `em`, `%`, `vw`, `vh`, `fr`, `ch`. `rem` follows the system's text scale like a browser's font size (`text-*` and `p-4` grow with it, px values do not; `App.IgnoreTextScale` opts out). `calc()` only as `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()` and `a ± b`.

**Variants** (stack them: `dark:md:hover:bg-zinc-800`):
- State: `hover:` `active:` `focus:` `focus-visible:` `focus-within:` `disabled:` `enabled:` `checked:`, text fields `placeholder:` `invalid:` `read-only:` `placeholder-shown:` `selection:`.
- ARIA: `aria-checked:` `aria-selected:` `aria-expanded:` `aria-pressed:` `aria-invalid:` `aria-disabled:` `aria-busy:` `aria-hidden:` `aria-required:` `aria-readonly:` (they match the element's own `h.Aria...(true)` prop), `aria-[current=page]:` (also `step`, `location`, `date`, `time`, `true`; there is no bare `aria-current:`), `aria-[sort=ascending]:`/`descending`.
- Structure: `first:` `last:` `only:` `odd:` `even:` (the place among the element's own siblings: don't wrap items in a keyed `Div` just for the key, use `Key(...)` or `tela.WithKey`, which add no element); `group` + `group-hover:`/`group-focus-within:`/`group-aria-*:` on descendants; `peer` + `peer-checked:`/`peer-invalid:`... on following siblings (no named groups).
- Environment: `dark:`, `sm:` `md:` `lg:` `xl:` `2xl:` (window at least 640/768/1024/1280/1536 px), `max-md:` ..., `min-[600px]:`, `max-[40rem]:`, `motion-reduce:`, `motion-safe:`, `contrast-more:` (the system asks for high contrast), `rtl:`/`ltr:`, `starting:` (entrance: the style a newly shown element transitions from, CSS `@starting-style`).

```go
func NavLink(label string, current bool, onClick func()) tela.Node {
	page := ""
	if current {
		page = "page"
	}
	return Button(AriaCurrent(page), OnClick(onClick),
		Class("group flex h-9 w-full items-center gap-3 rounded-md px-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground transition-colors",
			"hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground",
			"aria-[current=page]:bg-accent aria-[current=page]:font-medium aria-[current=page]:text-foreground"),
		Icon(lucide.Bell, Class("size-4 group-hover:text-foreground")), Text(label))
}

func Toast(message string) tela.Node {
	// Fades and slides in when it appears; under Presence, Exit classes run when it is removed.
	return Div(Class("rounded-lg border border-border bg-popover px-4 py-3 text-sm shadow-lg transition duration-300",
		"starting:translate-y-2 starting:opacity-0"), Exit("translate-y-2 opacity-0"), Role("status"), Text(message))
}

func Responsive() tela.Node {
	return Div(Class("grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 p-4 md:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-3"),
		Div(Class("h-24 rounded-xl bg-linear-to-br from-sky-400 to-indigo-600 shadow-lg dark:from-sky-600 dark:to-indigo-900")),
		Div(Class("h-24 rounded-xl bg-white/60 ring-1 ring-black/5 backdrop-blur dark:bg-white/5 dark:ring-white/10")))
}
```

**Theme tokens** (shadcn/ui names) work in every color utility (`bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `fill-`, `stroke-`, `shadow-`...), with opacity (`bg-primary/90`, `ring-ring/50`) and variants, and follow the color scheme by themselves: no `dark:` pairs needed. Tokens: `background`, `foreground`, `card`, `card-foreground`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `destructive`, `border`, `input`, `ring`, `chart-1`..`chart-5`. Give the window `RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground"`. Palette colors (`bg-zinc-900`) do not follow the scheme: pair them with `dark:`.

`kit.Theme()` is shadcn's neutral theme with its 10 px radius (`rounded-lg` = 10 px, `rounded-md` 8, `rounded-xl` 14); `tela.DefaultTheme()` has the same colors with Tailwind's radius scale. Change colors, add your own tokens, alias class combinations:

```go
var brandTheme = func() tela.Theme {
	t := kit.Theme()
	t.Colors["primary"] = tela.SchemeColor{Light: tela.Hex("#4f46e5"), Dark: tela.Hex("#818cf8")}
	t.Colors["primary-foreground"] = tela.SchemeColor{Light: tela.Hex("#ffffff"), Dark: tela.Hex("#1e1b4b")}
	t.Colors["brand"] = tela.SchemeColor{Light: tela.Hex("#7c3aed"), Dark: tela.Hex("#a78bfa")} // bg-brand, text-brand...
	t.FontSans = "Geist"                                                                         // a system font
	return t
}()

var BrandApp = tela.App{
	Title: "Notes", Theme: &brandTheme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	ClassAliases: map[string]string{
		"text-muted": "text-sm text-muted-foreground",
		"eyebrow":    "text-xs font-semibold tracking-wide text-brand uppercase",
	},
	Root: P(Class("eyebrow"), Text("Notes")),
}
```

Colors in Go: `tela.Hex("#4f46e5")`, `tela.RGB`, `tela.RGBA(r, g, b, a)`, `tela.OKLCH(l, c, h)`, `tela.UseTheme().Color("primary")`. `h.Scheme(tela.Dark)` gives a subtree its own scheme (a dark sidebar in a light app). `tela.SetColorScheme(tela.Dark)` switches the app's scheme at run time, and `tela.SetTheme(t)` its theme: an accent picker copies `kit.Theme()`, sets `t.Colors["primary"]` (and `ring`) and calls `tela.SetTheme(t)`, so every `bg-primary` follows.

**Fonts:** text uses the system's fonts; none are in the binary. `font-sans` is `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif`. To fix the look: `tela.App{Fonts: []tela.Font{inter.Sans}}` (`fonts/inter`, 1.8 MB) or your files, `tela.FontData("Lora", ttf)` / `tela.FontFS(fsys, "Lora", "fonts/*.ttf")` plus `.Sans()`, `.Serif()`, `.Mono()`, `.Scripts("Hebr")`; app fonts come first. Tests, snapshots and mcp use the App's fonts, then Inter, Source Serif 4 and JetBrains Mono, never the system's (`telatest.Fonts`).

**Icons:** `Icon(lucide.Settings, Class("size-4"))`. An icon is 1em square (follows `text-*` size) unless sized, colored by the text color (`text-muted-foreground`), `stroke-[1.5]` thins it; decorative unless it has an `AriaLabel`. Lucide names are the file names of lucide.dev in PascalCase (`arrow-up-right` is `lucide.ArrowUpRight`, `circle-alert` is `lucide.CircleAlert`); to check one, `go doc github.com/kuronosu/tela/icons/lucide CircleAlert` (an old name such as `AlertCircle` compiles and its doc says what replaces it). Your own SVGs: `tela.Icon{SVG: "<svg ...>"}`, `tela.MustSVG(data)`, or `tela icons gen -pkg icons -o ./icons ./svg` for a whole directory.

**Not implemented** (you get a dev error that says what to use): floats and `clear` (use flex/grid); margin collapsing (use `gap`/`space-y-*`); `display: table` and `border-collapse` (use `kit.Table` or grid); `space-*-reverse`; `columns-*`; pseudo-elements `before:` `after:` `marker:` `file:` (use nodes); `data-*:`, `has-*:`, `not-*:`, `nth-*:`, `*:`, `[&...]:`, `@container`/`@md:`, `print:`, `supports-*:`; CSS variables other than the theme's own (`var(--color-<token>)`, `var(--radius)`, `var(--radius-<size>)`, `var(--spacing)`; an app's `--foo` is an error); arbitrary properties other than `[clip-path:...]`; 3D transforms; `scroll-snap`, `scroll-m-*`; `text-indent`; `hyphens`; `accent-*`; `resize`; `bg-fixed`; `vertical-align` on spans; custom `@keyframes` (use the `animate-*` classes, springs or `tela.Animate`); `content-box`.

## 6. kit: components in shadcn/ui's look

`kit` has 37 components with shadcn/ui's ("new-york-v4") look, built on the `aria` behavior hooks: keyboard, focus and roles are done. Use them for every control; build layout and decoration with `h` elements and classes around them.

**Rules that hold for every component:**
- Each is a struct; its fields are its props. `Class` adds classes to the root after the component's own (last wins: `Class: "w-full"` overrides); parts have `...Class` fields (`HeaderClass`, `ContentClass`, `ItemClass`...). `Props` takes one more `h` prop for the root (`Props: TestID("save")`; several: `tela.MergeProps(TestID("x"), AutoComplete("email"))`).
- Content is `Children tela.Component`; multi-part components have slots (`kit.Card{Title, Description, Action, Children, Footer}`). Text-only slots for assistive technologies are strings (`kit.Field{Label, Description, Error}`).
- A kit component is a `tela.Node`: return it from a function or a `Build` as it is (`return kit.Button{...}`); `Fragment` is only for several siblings.
- Values: controlled `Value *T` + `OnValueChange func(T)` (`Checked *bool` + `OnCheckedChange`, `Open *bool` + `OnOpenChange`, `Pressed`), or uncontrolled `DefaultValue`/`DefaultChecked`/`DefaultOpen`. Choices among keys are generic: `kit.Select[string]`, `Value *K`, `DefaultValue *K` (write `new("pro")`: `new` takes a value since Go 1.26).
- `Variant`: `kit.Default` (zero), `kit.Secondary`, `kit.Outline`, `kit.Ghost`, `kit.Destructive`, `kit.Link` (and `kit.TabsLine` for Tabs). `Size`: empty is the default size, then `kit.Xs`, `kit.Sm`, `kit.Lg`, and for icon-only buttons `kit.Icon`, `kit.IconXs`, `kit.IconSm`, `kit.IconLg`. `Orientation`: `kit.Horizontal`, `kit.Vertical`. An undefined variant or size panics in dev mode with the valid ones.
- Overlays (`Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Popover`, `Tooltip`, menus, pickers) take a `Trigger`: a `kit.Button{...}`, or any element through `kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node { return Button(p, ...) })`. Put `Disabled` on the overlay, not on its trigger. A trigger takes one overlay.
- Icons are `tela.Icon` fields (`Button.Icon`, `IconEnd`), defaulting to Lucide's where shadcn draws one.
- Customize: theme tokens first; then recipes: `s := kit.DefaultStyle()`, edit class strings (`s.Card.Root += " shadow-lg"`, `s.Button.Variants["glass"] = "bg-white/10 text-white hover:bg-white/20"`), apply with `kit.StyleProvider{Style: &s, Children: ...}`; then per instance `Class`.

**Catalog** (key fields; nearly every component also has `Class` and `Props`):

- `kit.Button{Variant, Size, Icon, IconEnd, Type, Disabled, OnClick, AriaLabel, Children}`: `Type: "submit"` in a `Form`; icon-only buttons need `Size: kit.Icon` and `AriaLabel`.
- `kit.Badge{Variant, Icon, Children}`: a small label.
- `kit.Card{Title, Description, Action, Children, Footer, TitleLevel, HeaderClass, ContentClass, FooterClass}`: the surface; `TitleLevel: 2` makes the title an `h2`; `Action` sits at the header's end.
- `kit.Avatar{Src, Alt, Fallback, Size, FallbackClass}`: `Src: SrcPath("img/ada.png")`; `Fallback` initials.
- `kit.Separator{Orientation, Semantic}`: a 1 px line (`Semantic` puts it in the accessibility tree).
- `kit.Skeleton{Class}`: a pulsing placeholder (`Class: "h-4 w-40 rounded-md"`).
- `kit.Label{For, Disabled, Children}`: a styled label for a control with an `ID`.
- `kit.Input{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Type, Placeholder, Name, ID, AriaLabel, Disabled, ReadOnly, Invalid, AutoFocus, MaxLength}`.
- `kit.Textarea{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder, Rows, MaxLength, AriaLabel, Invalid}`.
- `kit.Field{Label, Description, Error, Invalid, Orientation, ControlAfter, Children, LabelClass, ContentClass}`: label, control, help and error wired together (`Error` marks the control invalid). One kit control per field: not a trigger (`AlertDialog`, `Dialog`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu`), which names nothing (lint says so); a "label + button" row is plain elements, see the pattern below. Its spacing, to match it in rows you build by hand: `gap-3` between label, control and description; in a horizontal field the label and description are a column with `gap-1.5`; the description is `text-sm text-muted-foreground`.
- `kit.FieldSet{Legend, LegendVariant, Description, Children, LegendClass, ContentClass}`: a named group; names a `RadioGroup`/`ToggleGroup` inside. `LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel` is label-sized, the default `kit.LegendVariantLegend` a title.
- `kit.Checkbox{Checked, DefaultChecked, OnCheckedChange, Disabled, Required, Invalid, ID, AriaLabel}`.
- `kit.Switch{Checked, DefaultChecked, OnCheckedChange, Size, Disabled, ID, AriaLabel, ThumbClass}`.
- `kit.RadioGroup[K]{Items, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Orientation, Disabled, AriaLabel, Render, OptionClass}`: options are `kit.RadioItem[K]{Value, Label, Description, Disabled}`; `Render func(kit.RadioItem[K], kit.RadioState) tela.Node` draws an option yourself (cards).
- `kit.RadioState{Checked, Disabled, Invalid, ID, Props, Indicator}`: what `Render` gets: put `Props` on the one element that is the radio; `Indicator` is the default circle.
- `kit.Toggle{Pressed, DefaultPressed, OnPressedChange, Variant, Size, Icon, AriaLabel, Children}`: a button that stays pressed.
- `kit.ToggleGroup[K]{Items, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Multiple, Selected, OnSelectionChange, DisallowEmptySelection, Variant, Size, Spacing, AriaLabel, ItemClass}`: segmented control; items `kit.ToggleGroupItem[K]{Value, Label, Icon, AriaLabel, Disabled}`.
- `kit.Slider{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Values, OnValuesChange, Min, Max, Step, Orientation, Disabled, AriaLabel, FormatValue}`: `Value *float64`; `DefaultValue: new(50.0)`; `FormatValue func(float64) string` is the value as read aloud (aria-valuetext), not drawn: show the value yourself (`Textf("%g px", v)`).
- `kit.Progress{Value, Max, Indeterminate, AriaLabel}`: `Value` is a plain number (0 to `Max`, 100 by default).
- `kit.Select[K]{Items, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder, Size, Disabled, Invalid, AriaLabel, ID}`: items `kit.SelectItem[K]{Value, Label, Icon, Disabled, Group}`; its trigger is a `button` named "chosen label + field label".
- `kit.Tabs[K]{Tabs, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Orientation, Variant, AriaLabel, ListClass, TriggerClass, ContentClass}`: `kit.Tab[K]{Value, Label, Icon, Disabled, Content}`; only the selected panel is built.
- `kit.Table[T]{Rows, RowKey, Columns, Sort, DefaultSort, OnSortChange, Selected, RowProps, Caption, AriaLabel, Empty, RowHeight}`: columns `kit.Column[T]{Header, Cell, Sort, Width, Align, Sticky, Footer}`; `Width string` is the column's grid track (`"200px"`, `"1fr"`, `"auto"`, `"minmax(120px, 1fr)"`); `Align: kit.AlignRight`; a `Sort` func makes a header sortable. `RowHeight: 37` (px) makes the table virtual for thousands of rows (only the rows in view exist; give it a height, px/fr/minmax widths, no Sticky).
- `kit.Dialog{Trigger, Title, Description, Children, Footer, Open, DefaultOpen, OnOpenChange, HideClose, AriaLabel}`: modal; Escape and the scrim close it.
- `kit.AlertDialog{Trigger, Title, Description, Cancel, Action, Destructive, OnAction, OnCancel, Open, OnOpenChange, Disabled}`: a confirmation. `Title`, `Description`, `Cancel` and `Action` are `tela.Component`s, not strings: `Title: Text("Delete?")`, `Cancel: Text("Keep editing")`, `Action: Text("Delete")` (defaults "Cancel" and "Continue"). `Disabled` goes here, not on the trigger.
- `kit.Popover{Trigger, Children, Placement, Align, Offset, Modal, AriaLabel, Open, OnOpenChange}`: non-modal panel; `Placement: "top"`, `Align: "start"`.
- `kit.TitleBar{Variant, Look, Title, Leading, Children, Trailing, ControlsSide, HideMinimize, HideMaximize, State, TitleClass}`: the title bar of a `Frameless` window (or one with `tela.UseWindow().State().ClientSideDecorations`): a drag area (`h.WindowDrag`) with a title, slots and the window controls at the platform's side; buttons and fields in the slots stay clickable. Looks `kit.Windows`, `kit.GNOME`, `kit.MacOS` (default by OS), and `kit.Plain` for an app with a design of its own: the platform's arrangement (`Look` picks another) with no background, border or outline (add `Class: "bg-sidebar"` for a surface) and ghost window controls in the theme's tokens; it dims when the window is unfocused and drops its outline when maximized. Put it at the top of a flex column.
- `kit.WindowControls{Variant, Look, HideMinimize, HideMaximize, State, MinimizeLabel, MaximizeLabel, RestoreLabel, CloseLabel}`: minimize, maximize/restore and close as real buttons (named "Minimize", "Maximize"/"Restore", "Close") that act on click; `Variant: kit.Plain` draws them quietly (ghost buttons; `Look` picks the arrangement); `TitleBar` draws them, so use this alone only to place them yourself.
- `kit.Tooltip{Trigger, Content, Placement, Delay, Disabled}`: on hover or keyboard focus; describes its trigger.
- `kit.DropdownMenu[K]{Trigger, Items, OnSelect, Placement, Align, AriaLabel, Open, OnOpenChange}`: items `kit.MenuItem[K]{Kind, Key, Label, Icon, Shortcut, Variant, Disabled, OnSelect, Checked, DefaultChecked, OnCheckedChange, Items}`; `Kind`: `kit.MenuPlain` (zero), `kit.MenuCheckbox`, `kit.MenuRadioGroup`, `kit.MenuLabel`, `kit.MenuSeparator`, `kit.MenuGroup`. No submenus.
- `kit.ContextMenu[K]{Children, Items, OnSelect, AriaLabel, Disabled, Native}`: right click (or long press) on `Children`. `Native: kit.NativeOn` uses the OS's menu where there is one (section 8).
- `kit.Menubar[K]{Menus, OnSelect, AriaLabel, Native, AppMenu, AppItems}`: menus `kit.MenubarMenu[K]{Key, Label, Items, Disabled, Role}` (`Role: desktop.RoleEditMenu` with no Items: the OS's Edit menu in a native bar). `AppMenu` makes it the app's one bar (see Native menus).
- `kit.Toaster{Children, Position, Duration, VisibleToasts, CloseButton}`: put once around the app; any component below calls `toast := kit.UseToast()` (a `kit.ToastHandle`: comparable, safe to keep in a struct field or pass to a helper) then `toast.Success(title, opts...)`, `Error`, `Info`, `Warning`, `Loading`, `Show`, `Dismiss(id)`; options `kit.ToastDescription(text)`, `kit.ToastAction(label, fn)`, `kit.ToastDuration(d)`, `kit.ToastReplace(id)`. Safe from any goroutine.
- `kit.Calendar{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Min, Max, IsDateUnavailable, VisibleMonths}`: one `aria.Date` (comparable day, zero = none; `aria.Today()`).
- `kit.RangeCalendar{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, VisibleMonths}`: an `aria.DateRange`.
- `kit.DatePicker{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder, Min, Max}`: an outline button that opens a calendar.
- `kit.DateRangePicker{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder}`: the same for a range.
- `kit.ColorPicker{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, OnValueCommit, Alpha, Swatches}`: a `tela.Color` (`DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))`).
- `kit.ColorInput{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Swatches}`: the picker behind a button.
- `kit.StyleProvider{Style, Children}`: applies an edited `kit.DefaultStyle()` to a subtree.

**Patterns.** A form card with fields, errors and a submit:

```go
func Profile() tela.Node { return tela.C(profile) }

func profile() tela.Node {
	name, setName := tela.UseState("Ada Lovelace")
	email, setEmail := tela.UseState("ada@example")
	bio, setBio := tela.UseState("")
	emailError := ""
	if !strings.Contains(email, ".") {
		emailError = "Enter a valid e-mail address."
	}
	return kit.Card{
		Class: "w-full max-w-md", TitleLevel: 2,
		Title:       Text("Profile"),
		Description: Text("This is how others see you."),
		Action:      kit.Badge{Variant: kit.Secondary, Children: Text("Public")},
		Children: Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-5"),
			kit.Field{Label: "Name", Children: kit.Input{Value: &name, OnValueChange: setName.Set}},
			kit.Field{Label: "E-mail", Description: "We never share it.", Error: emailError,
				Children: kit.Input{Type: "email", Value: &email, OnValueChange: setEmail.Set}},
			kit.Field{Label: "Bio", Children: kit.Textarea{Rows: 3, Placeholder: "A few words", Value: &bio, OnValueChange: setBio.Set}}),
		FooterClass: "justify-end gap-2",
		Footer: Fragment(
			kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: Text("Cancel")},
			kit.Button{Disabled: emailError != "", Children: Text("Save")}),
	}
}
```

Switch rows, a radio group named by a legend, radio cards, a select, a segmented control:

```go
func Preferences() tela.Node { return tela.C(preferences) }

func preferences() tela.Node {
	digest, setDigest := tela.UseState(true)
	plan, setPlan := tela.UseState("pro")
	size, setSize := tela.UseState("md")
	view, setView := tela.UseState("list")
	plans := []kit.RadioItem[string]{
		{Value: "free", Label: "Free", Description: "Up to 3 projects."},
		{Value: "pro", Label: "Pro", Description: "Unlimited projects."},
	}
	return Div(Class("flex max-w-lg flex-col gap-6"),
		// A switch row: text first, the switch at the end.
		kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Class: "items-center gap-6",
			Label: "Weekly digest", Description: "A summary every Monday.",
			Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &digest, OnCheckedChange: setDigest.Set}},
		// The legend names the group: no AriaLabel needed.
		kit.FieldSet{Legend: "Plan", LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
			Children: kit.RadioGroup[string]{Items: plans, Value: &plan, OnValueChange: setPlan.Set}},
		kit.Field{Label: "Text size", Children: kit.Select[string]{Class: "w-40", Value: &size, OnValueChange: setSize.Set,
			Items: []kit.SelectItem[string]{{Value: "sm", Label: "Small"}, {Value: "md", Label: "Medium"}, {Value: "lg", Label: "Large"}}}},
		kit.FieldSet{Legend: "View", LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
			Children: kit.ToggleGroup[string]{Variant: kit.Outline, DisallowEmptySelection: true, Value: &view, OnValueChange: setView.Set,
				Items: []kit.ToggleGroupItem[string]{{Value: "list", Label: "List"}, {Value: "grid", Label: "Grid"}}}},
		// Radio cards: Render draws each option; st.Props makes the button the radio.
		kit.RadioGroup[string]{AriaLabel: "Plan cards", Items: plans, Value: &plan, OnValueChange: setPlan.Set, Class: "grid-cols-2",
			Render: func(o kit.RadioItem[string], st kit.RadioState) tela.Node {
				return Button(Key(o.Value), st.Props,
					Class("flex flex-col items-start gap-1 rounded-lg border border-border p-4 text-left transition-colors hover:bg-accent",
						"aria-checked:border-primary aria-checked:ring-1 aria-checked:ring-primary"),
					Div(Class("flex items-center gap-2 text-sm font-medium"), st.Indicator, Text(o.Label)),
					P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text(o.Description)))
			}},
	)
}
```

Tabs, buttons, an alert dialog, a toast, a tooltip, a dropdown menu, an avatar:

```go
func Account() tela.Node { return kit.Toaster{Children: tela.C(account)} }

func account() tela.Node {
	toast := kit.UseToast()
	menu := []kit.MenuItem[string]{
		{Kind: kit.MenuLabel, Label: "My account"},

			kit.Avatar{Fallback: "AL", Size: kit.Lg},

			kit.DropdownMenu[string]{Align: "end", Items: menu, OnSelect: func(k string) { toast.Info("Chose " + k) },

		kit.Separator{},

				kit.Button{Variant: kit.Link, Children: Text("Learn more")})},

					Title:       Text("Delete your account?"),
					Description: Text("This cannot be undone."),
					Action:      Text("Delete"), Destructive: true,
					OnAction: func() { toast.Error("Account deleted") },
				})},
		}})

```

A table and a dialog with a form:

```go
type Invoice struct {
	ID, Status string
	Amount     float64
}

func Invoices(rows []Invoice) tela.Node {
	return kit.Table[Invoice]{
		Rows: rows, RowKey: func(i Invoice) any { return i.ID }, Caption: "Recent invoices",
		Columns: []kit.Column[Invoice]{
			{Header: "Invoice", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return Span(Class("font-medium"), Text(i.ID)) },
				Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) }},
			{Header: "Status", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return kit.Badge{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: Text(i.Status)} }},
			{Header: "Amount", Align: kit.AlignRight, Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return Textf("$%.2f", i.Amount) },
				Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return cmp.Compare(a.Amount, b.Amount) }},
		},
	}
}

func Rename() tela.Node { return tela.C(rename) }

func rename() tela.Node {
	open, setOpen := tela.UseState(false)
	name, setName := tela.UseState("Roadmap")
	return kit.Dialog{
		Open: &open, OnOpenChange: setOpen.Set,
		Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Icon: lucide.Pencil, Children: Text("Rename")},
		Title:       Text("Rename project"),
		Description: Text("Pick a short, memorable name."),
		Children:    kit.Field{Label: "Name", Children: kit.Input{Value: &name, OnValueChange: setName.Set, AutoFocus: true}},
		Footer:      kit.Button{Disabled: name == "", OnClick: func() { setOpen.Set(false) }, Children: Text("Save")},
	}
}
```

		Class("flex flex-col gap-0.5 rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/5 px-4 py-3 text-sm text-destructive"),
