## 7. A complete settings screen

A compact, complete screen (one file, `package main`): an app shell with a sidebar whose current item has `AriaCurrent("page")`, a header with Save, a card of switch rows, a card with a `FieldSet` of radio cards and a horizontal `Field` with a `Select`; Save applies the theme with `tela.SetColorScheme` and shows a toast. It uses tokens only, so dark mode needs no `dark:` class. Copy its structure: `max-w-3xl` centered content, `gap-6` between cards, `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight` title with a `text-sm text-muted-foreground` subtitle, rows separated by `border-t first:border-t-0`. `examples/settings` is a larger screen built by an LLM from this guide and a prompt (in its README): five sections, validation, confirmations, an accent picked at run time.

```go
// Command settings is a settings screen on kit: an app shell with a sidebar
// and a page of switches, radio cards and a select.
package main

import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/icons/lucide"
)

// Prefs is the whole form: comparable, so prefs != saved means "unsaved".
type Prefs struct {
	Email, Push, Digest bool
	Theme, Language     string
}

var defaults = Prefs{Email: true, Push: true, Theme: "system", Language: "en"}

type navItem struct {
	Label string
	Icon  tela.Icon
}

var nav = []navItem{
	{"Dashboard", lucide.LayoutDashboard}, {"Projects", lucide.FolderKanban},
	{"Team", lucide.Users}, {"Settings", lucide.Settings},
}

var themes = []kit.RadioItem[string]{
	{Value: "light", Label: "Light"}, {Value: "dark", Label: "Dark"}, {Value: "system", Label: "System"},
}

var themeIcons = map[string]tela.Icon{"light": lucide.Sun, "dark": lucide.Moon, "system": lucide.Monitor}

var schemes = map[string]tela.ColorScheme{"light": tela.Light, "dark": tela.Dark, "system": tela.System}

var languages = []kit.SelectItem[string]{
	{Value: "en", Label: "English"}, {Value: "es", Label: "Español"},
	{Value: "fr", Label: "Français"}, {Value: "de", Label: "Deutsch"},
}

// Settings is the screen; tela.C gives settings its own hook state.
func Settings() tela.Node { return tela.C(settings) }

func settings() tela.Node {
	page, setPage := tela.UseState("Settings")
	prefs, setPrefs := tela.UseState(defaults)
	saved, setSaved := tela.UseState(defaults)
	toast := kit.UseToast()

	edit := func(f func(p *Prefs)) { setPrefs.Update(func(p Prefs) Prefs { f(&p); return p }) }
	save := func() {
		setSaved.Set(prefs)
		tela.SetColorScheme(schemes[prefs.Theme])
		toast.Success("Settings saved", kit.ToastDescription("Your preferences were updated."))
	}
	row := func(label, hint string, on bool, set func(p *Prefs, on bool)) tela.Node {
		return kit.Field{
			Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Label: label, Description: hint,
			Class:    "items-center gap-6 border-t border-border py-4 first:border-t-0 first:pt-0 last:pb-0",
			Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &on, OnCheckedChange: func(v bool) { edit(func(p *Prefs) { set(p, v) }) }},
		}
	}

	sidebar := Div(Role("navigation"), AriaLabel("Main"),
		Class("flex w-60 shrink-0 flex-col gap-1 border-r border-border bg-muted/40 p-3"),
		Div(Class("flex items-center gap-2.5 px-2 pt-1 pb-5"),
			Div(Class("flex size-8 items-center justify-center rounded-lg bg-primary text-primary-foreground"),
				Icon(lucide.Layers, Class("size-4"))),
			Span(Class("font-semibold tracking-tight"), Text("Acme"))),
		Map(nav, func(n navItem) tela.Node {
			current := ""
			if n.Label == page {
				current = "page"
			}
			return Button(Key(n.Label), AriaCurrent(current), OnClick(func() { setPage.Set(n.Label) }),
				Class("flex h-9 items-center gap-3 rounded-md px-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground transition-colors",
					"hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground",
					"aria-[current=page]:bg-accent aria-[current=page]:font-medium aria-[current=page]:text-foreground"),
				Icon(n.Icon, Class("size-4")), Text(n.Label))
		}),
		Div(Class("mt-auto flex items-center gap-3 border-t border-border px-2 pt-4"),
			kit.Avatar{Fallback: "AL"},
			Div(Class("flex min-w-0 flex-col text-sm"),
				Span(Class("font-medium"), Text("Ada Lovelace")),
				Span(Class("truncate text-xs text-muted-foreground"), Text("ada@example.com")))),
	)

	content := Div(Class("mx-auto flex max-w-3xl flex-col gap-6 px-8 py-8"),
		Div(Class("flex items-end justify-between gap-4"),
			Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-1"),
				H1(Class("text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight"), Text("Settings")),
				P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text("Manage your notifications and how Acme looks."))),
			kit.Button{Icon: lucide.Check, Disabled: prefs == saved, OnClick: save, Children: Text("Save changes")}),
		kit.Card{TitleLevel: 2, Title: Text("Notifications"), Description: Text("Choose what we tell you about."),
			Children: Div(Class("flex flex-col"),
				row("Email notifications", "A summary of activity in your workspace.", prefs.Email, func(p *Prefs, v bool) { p.Email = v }),
				row("Push notifications", "Mentions and replies, on your devices.", prefs.Push, func(p *Prefs, v bool) { p.Push = v }),
				row("Weekly digest", "A Monday recap of what your team shipped.", prefs.Digest, func(p *Prefs, v bool) { p.Digest = v }))},
		kit.Card{TitleLevel: 2, Title: Text("Appearance"), Description: Text("Applied when you save."),
			ContentClass: "flex flex-col gap-6",
			Children: Fragment(
				kit.FieldSet{Legend: "Theme", LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
					Children: kit.RadioGroup[string]{Items: themes, Render: themeCard, Class: "grid-cols-3",
						Value: &prefs.Theme, OnValueChange: func(v string) { edit(func(p *Prefs) { p.Theme = v }) }}},
				kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Class: "items-center gap-6",
					Label: "Language", Description: "Used for dates, numbers and messages.",
					Children: kit.Select[string]{Items: languages, Class: "w-44",
						Value: &prefs.Language, OnValueChange: func(v string) { edit(func(p *Prefs) { p.Language = v }) }}})},
	)

	return Div(Class("flex h-screen"), sidebar,
		Div(Class("min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto"),
			IfElse(page == "Settings", content, Div(Class("flex h-full items-center justify-center text-sm text-muted-foreground"),
				Textf("%s is empty in this example.", page)))))
}

// themeCard draws one theme option; st.Props makes the button the radio.
func themeCard(o kit.RadioItem[string], st kit.RadioState) tela.Node {
	return Button(Key(o.Value), st.Props,
		Class("flex items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-lg border border-border bg-card px-3 py-2.5 text-sm font-medium shadow-xs transition-colors",
			"hover:bg-accent focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50",
			"aria-checked:border-primary aria-checked:bg-accent aria-checked:ring-1 aria-checked:ring-primary"),
		Icon(themeIcons[o.Value], Class("size-4")), Text(o.Label))
}

var theme = kit.Theme()

// App is the window; tela snapshot, tela mcp and the tests mount it too.
var App = tela.App{
	Title: "Settings", Width: 1040, Height: 800,
	Theme: &theme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	Root: kit.Toaster{Children: Settings()},
}

func main() { tela.Main(App) }
```

Its aria snapshot (`tela inspect`, or the `snapshot` tool, which adds refs):

```yaml
- navigation "Main":
  - text: Acme
  - button "Dashboard"
  - button "Projects"
  - button "Team"
  - button "Settings"
  - text: AL Ada Lovelace ada@example.com
- heading "Settings" [level=1]
- paragraph: Manage your notifications and how Acme looks.
- button "Save changes" [disabled]
- heading "Notifications" [level=2]
- text: Choose what we tell you about.
- group:
  - text: Email notifications
  - paragraph: A summary of activity in your workspace.
  - switch "Email notifications" [checked]
...
- group "Theme":
  - text: Theme
  - radiogroup "Theme":
    - radio "Light"
    - radio "Dark"
    - radio "System" [checked]
- group:
  - text: Language
  - paragraph: Used for dates, numbers and messages.
  - button "English Language": English
- region "Notifications"
```

(`aria-current` is not printed in snapshots, as in Playwright; `region "Notifications"` is the Toaster's.)

## 8. Windows and desktop services

A window is state, like a dialog: a `tela.Window{...}` in the tree opens a window while it is mounted and closes it when it unmounts. All windows share one component tree, so a child window sees the state and contexts of the component that declares it (its `Root` is built by that component). Each window has its own layout, focus, hover and overlays. OS services (file dialogs, message boxes, notifications, tray, app folders, settings) are in package `github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop`.

- `tela.Window{Title, Width, Height, MinWidth..MaxHeight, FixedSize, Frameless, AlwaysOnTop, Modal, Hidden, Icon, RootClass, Placement, OnClose, Root}`. Keep "is it open" in `UseState` and render `If(open, tela.Window{...})`. `OnClose` runs when the user asks to close (close button, Alt+F4, `Close()`): set the state to false there. **A nil `OnClose` ignores the request**: the window cannot be closed (dev mode warns). `FixedSize`, `Frameless`, `Modal` and `Placement` are read when the window opens; `Hidden` keeps it open, with its state. `tela.App{OnQuit}` runs on Cmd+Q, the Dock or logout (nil: every window gets a close request; a tray app sets `OnQuit: tela.Quit`). A hidden or minimized window draws nothing but still builds and runs its effects, so a tray menu in it can follow `State().Hidden` ("Show"/"Hide"). On `tela.App` and `tela.Window`: `TitleBar: tela.TitleBarColors{Background, Text, Border}` colors Windows 11's title bar and border (zero = the system's); `Backdrop: tela.BackdropMica` (`BackdropMicaAlt`, `BackdropAcrylic`, `BackdropNone`) is the system material (Windows 11, macOS), shown where the root has no background (`RootClass` without `bg-background`, or `bg-background/60`).
- `tela.App` has the same fields for the main window, plus `AppID` and `OnClose func(tela.WindowHandle)`: nil quits when the main window closes; `func(w tela.WindowHandle) { w.Hide() }` keeps the app running (with a `desktop.Tray` as the way back). `tela.Quit()` ends the app from any goroutine; `tela.OpenURL(url)` and `tela.OpenPath(path)` open the default application.
- `tela.UseWindow()` returns the `tela.WindowHandle` of the window the component renders in: `Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Unmaximize`, `ToggleMaximize`, `SetFullscreen(bool)`, `Hide`, `Show`, `Focus`, `Close`, `State()` (`Maximized`, `Fullscreen`, `Minimized`, `Focused`, `Hidden`, `ClientSideDecorations`; reading it rebuilds the component when it changes) and `Placement()`. Requests are safe from any goroutine; the OS may refuse one (a tiling window manager does not maximize). In `tela snapshot` there is no window and the handle does nothing.
- **Custom title bar:** `Frameless: true`, and `kit.TitleBar{Title: Text("Notes"), Leading, Children, Trailing}` at the top of a flex column: it is the drag area and draws minimize, maximize and close (`kit.WindowControls`) in the OS's look; buttons and fields in its slots stay clickable. Without `kit`, mark the bar `h.WindowDrag()`, a plain area inside it that must not drag `h.WindowNoDrag()`, and real buttons `h.WindowControl(tela.WindowMinimize|WindowMaximize|WindowClose)` (with an `AriaLabel`); the OS does the move, the double click and the window menu. Without server-side decorations (GNOME on Wayland: `State().ClientSideDecorations`) Tela draws a fallback bar above the content; any `h.WindowDrag` area replaces it. `TitleBarOverlay: true` (App or Window) keeps the OS's buttons over the bar instead (macOS traffic lights; elsewhere it is `Frameless`): `kit.TitleBar` keeps room for `State().TitleBarControls` and draws no controls.

```go
package notes

import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"
)

var theme = kit.Theme()

// App: PersistApp reopens the main window where the user left it.
var App = desktop.PersistApp(tela.App{
	AppID: "com.example.notes", Title: "Notes", Width: 900, Height: 640,
	Frameless: true, Theme: &theme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	Root: Notes{},
})

type Notes struct{}

func (Notes) Build() tela.Node {
	prefs, setPrefs := tela.UseState(false)
	return Div(Class("flex h-screen flex-col"),
		kit.TitleBar{Title: Text("Notes")},
		Div(Class("min-h-0 grow p-4"),
			kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: Text("Preferences"),
				OnClick: func() { setPrefs.Set(true) }},
			If(prefs, tela.Window{
				Title: "Preferences", Width: 420, Height: 240, Modal: true,
				OnClose: func() { setPrefs.Set(false) },
				Root:    Preferences{},
			}),
		))
}

// Preferences is the content of the second window.
type Preferences struct{}

func (Preferences) Build() tela.Node {
	win := tela.UseWindow()
	dark, setDark := desktop.UseSetting("dark", false) // kept in the app's settings file
	return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-4 p-6"),
		kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Label: "Dark mode",
			Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &dark, OnCheckedChange: setDark.Set}},
		kit.Button{Children: Text("Done"), OnClick: win.Close})
}
```

**Desktop services** (`desktop`). Dialogs and notifications are asynchronous like a browser's: the call returns at once and the callback runs later **on the UI thread**, so it may set state. Call them from handlers and effects (from a goroutine, wrap the call in `tela.Post`; dev mode panics otherwise). Each returns an error when nothing was shown; it wraps `desktop.ErrUnsupported` when the desktop lacks the service (no XDG portal, no notification daemon, no tray host), and the app should fall back. In `tela snapshot` (no running app) they return an error.

- File dialogs: `desktop.OpenFile`, `OpenFiles`, `SaveFile`, `PickFolder(done, opts...)` with options `Title`, `Directory`, `DefaultName`, `Filter("Notes", "*.md", "*.txt")`, `Parent(win)`. `done(path, err)` gets `""` and a nil error when the user cancels. The dialog is modal to the window the call comes from.
- `desktop.ShowMessage(desktop.Message{Kind, Title, Text, Buttons, Parent}, func(desktop.Answer))`: kinds `MessageInfo/Warning/Error/Question`, buttons `ButtonsOK/OKCancel/YesNo/YesNoCancel`, answers `AnswerOK/Cancel/Yes/No`. Native on Windows; on Linux Tela draws it as a modal window. Escape or the close button answers Cancel (No for Yes/No).
- `desktop.Notify(desktop.Notification{Title, Body, Icon, Actions, OnClick, OnClose})` returns the shown notification (`Close()`). Windows shows no action buttons: keep every action reachable in the app. `Title` is required.
- `desktop.Tray{Icon, Tooltip, Menu, OnClick, OnError}` is a component: the icon is in the tray while it is mounted (`Icon` is one picture at several sizes, 16, 24 and 32 px; `Menu` is `[]desktop.MenuItem{Label, Separator, Checkbox, Checked, Disabled, Submenu, OnSelect}`; a checkbox item does not toggle itself). On GNOME without the AppIndicator extension `OnError` gets an `ErrUnsupported`: then do not hide the window on close.
- `desktop.UseSetting(key, def)` is `UseState` whose value lives in the app's JSON settings file (`desktop.Settings()` is the `*desktop.Store`: `Get`, `Set`, `Watch`). Values must encode as JSON; `def` is used only while the key has no stored value (or it no longer decodes); a stored value replaces it, except that a struct field the stored value lacks keeps `def`'s, while slice, array and map elements always start empty (an `omitempty` field an element omits is zero, not `def`'s).
- `desktop.PersistApp(app)` and `desktop.SavedWindow{Key, Window}` save and restore a window's size, maximized and fullscreen state and position. Wayland cannot place windows: only the size and state come back, and the position where the compositor restores sessions.
- Folders: `desktop.ConfigDir()`, `DataDir()`, `CacheDir()`, `StateDir()`, `LogDir()` (created on demand, named by `App.AppID` or `desktop.SetAppID("com.example.notes")`, called before the first read).

```go
package notes

import (
	"errors"
	"image"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
)

var trayIcon = []image.Image{image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 32, 32))} // the app's icon at 16, 24 and 32 px (decode embedded PNGs)

// Editor opens a file, asks before closing and lives in the tray.
func Editor() tela.Node {
	return tela.C(func() tela.Node {
		win := tela.UseWindow()
		path, setPath := tela.UseState("")
		typing, setTyping := tela.UseState(false) // fallback: a field for the path
		open := func() {
			err := desktop.OpenFile(func(p string, err error) {
				if err == nil && p != "" { // "" is cancel
					setPath.Set(p)
				}
			}, desktop.Title("Open a note"), desktop.Filter("Notes", "*.md", "*.txt"))
			if errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported) {
				setTyping.Set(true) // no portal in this session
			}
		}
		closeWindow := func() {
			desktop.ShowMessage(desktop.Message{
				Kind: desktop.MessageQuestion, Title: "Unsaved changes",
				Text: "Save the changes before closing?", Buttons: desktop.ButtonsYesNoCancel,
			}, func(a desktop.Answer) {
				if a != desktop.AnswerCancel {
					win.Hide() // the tray brings it back
				}
			})
		}
		return Div(
			desktop.Tray{
				Icon: trayIcon, Tooltip: "Notes", OnClick: win.Show,
				Menu: []desktop.MenuItem{
					{Label: "Show Notes", OnSelect: win.Show},
					{Separator: true},
					{Label: "Quit", OnSelect: tela.Quit},
				},
			},
			Button(OnClick(open), Text("Open…")),
			Button(OnClick(closeWindow), Text("Close")),
			If(typing, Input(Bind(path, setPath))),
			Text(path),
		)
	})
}
```

**Drag and drop, clipboard, shortcuts, launches, links, secrets, menus, settings.**

- **Drag and drop is HTML's.** A target takes `h.OnDragEnter`, `OnDragOver`, `OnDragLeave` and `OnDrop` (they bubble) and accepts by calling `e.PreventDefault()` in `OnDragOver`. Before the drop only the types are known (`e.DataTransfer.Has("Files")`, `Types()`); the data arrives in `OnDrop` (`Files()` absolute paths, `Text()`, `HTML()`, `Image()`, `GetData(mime)`). Enter fires on the new element before leave fires on the old one, so "a drag is over me" is a counter (+1 on enter, -1 on leave, 0 on drop). A source is `h.Draggable(true)`: its `OnDragStart` fills `e.DataTransfer` (`SetText`, `SetHTML`, `SetFiles`, `SetImage`, `SetData(mime, s)`, `EffectAllowed = tela.DropMove`); with no data the press stays the `OnDrag` gesture. `OnDragEnd` reads `e.DataTransfer.DropEffect` (`tela.DropNone|DropCopy|DropMove|DropLink`). It works between windows and with other apps.
- **Clipboard:** `desktop.ReadClipboard(done, types...)` (`done(*tela.DataTransfer, err)` on the UI thread) and `desktop.WriteClipboard(&dt)` (every representation at once) carry the same `DataTransfer`; `ReadClipboardText` and `WriteClipboardText` for text only. Text fields keep their own paste.
- **`desktop.GlobalShortcut{ID, Keys, Description, OnPress, OnRelease, OnStatus}`** is a component: the shortcut is registered while it is mounted (keep `ID` stable; several allowed). The OS decides, so show `OnStatus`: `ShortcutBound` (`Trigger` is what the user presses: the Wayland portal asks the user and may bind other keys; `""` on Hyprland, which assigns none: the user adds `bind = CTRL ALT, N, global, <AppID>:<ID>` to hyprland.conf), `ShortcutTaken`, `ShortcutRefused`, `ShortcutRevoked`, `ShortcutFailed` (`Err` wraps `ErrUnsupported` when the desktop has none, `ErrAppNotRegistered` without the app's desktop entry). Check `Keys` typed by a user with `desktop.ParseKeys`.
- **`desktop.RegisterApp()`** in `main`, before `tela.Run`, in the built program (give the app an `AppID`): the Linux shortcut portal needs the app's desktop entry. It writes only that entry (per user, no menu launcher), nothing when it is there or another program's is; nothing on Windows. `UnregisterApp`, `AppStatus`.
- **One instance and launches:** `desktop.SingleInstance(app)` (needs `AppID`) makes a second start forward its arguments to the running app and exit with status 0; the running app raises its main window (shown, from the tray too). `desktop.UseLaunch(func(desktop.Launch))` is a hook that gets the process's own start once and every forwarded start; `l.URLs()` (`notes:open?id=3`), `l.Files()` (absolute paths).
- **Links and file types:** `desktop.Register(desktop.URLScheme("notes"))` and `desktop.FileType(".note", "application/x-notes-note", "Notes document")` make the app a *candidate* handler, per user and without a running app (an installer can call it); `changed` is false when nothing was written. It **does not make the app the default** (that is `desktop.MakeDefault`, only when the user asks; for Windows file types it opens Settings and returns `DefaultAsked`) and **never takes another app's association** (`ErrAssociationTaken` unless you pass `desktop.Replace()`, after asking). `desktop.RegistrationStatus` says `Registered`, `Default` and `Other`; `Unregister` removes it. It does file or registry I/O: call it at start or off the UI thread. Under `go run` or `tela dev` the executable is temporary: give `desktop.ForApp(desktop.HandlerApp{Exec: path})` or skip (`ErrDevExecutable`).
- **Secrets:** `desktop.SetSecret(name, []byte)`, `Secret(name)`, `DeleteSecret(name)` use the OS keyring (Credential Manager, Secret Service, Keychain), per app ID. They block (the OS may ask the user to unlock the keyring): **call them from a goroutine, never from a handler or an effect** (dev mode warns). Errors: `ErrSecretNotFound`, `ErrSecretCanceled` (the user dismissed the prompt; do not retry in a loop), `ErrUnsupported` (no keyring: turn the feature off).
- **Trash:** `desktop.MoveToTrash(path)` moves a file or folder to the trash (Recycle Bin), never deleting it: a file the trash cannot take stays and the error wraps `ErrUnsupported`; a missing one wraps `fs.ErrNotExist`. It blocks: ask the user first, then call it from a goroutine and `tela.Post` the outcome.
- **Native menus:** `kit.ContextMenu` and `kit.Menubar` are drawn by default. `Native: kit.NativeOn` (or `kit.NativeOff`) per menu, or `tela.App{NativeMenus: true}` for all (a menu's own setting wins), uses the OS's menu where there is one (Windows now: context menus, and a menu bar on windows with a title bar of the OS) and draws it elsewhere (Linux, frameless windows), with no code of yours. A native menu drops icons, the destructive color, `KeepOpen` and classes. Below kit: `desktop.PopupMenu(win, at, items, done)` and `desktop.MenuBar{Menus, OnError}` return or report `ErrUnsupported` so you can draw your own. **The app's menu bar**, declared once anywhere: `desktop.AppMenuBar{Menus, AppItems, OnError}` or `kit.Menubar{AppMenu: true, AppItems}`: macOS's bar for every window (`AppItems` go in the app menu), on Windows the bar of every framed window without its own `desktop.MenuBar` (which macOS lacks), else `ErrUnsupported` and kit draws it. `desktop.MenuItem{Role: desktop.RoleCopy}` (Electron's roles: undo, redo, cut, paste, selectAll, minimize, zoom, close) gets label and action, `{Role: desktop.RoleEditMenu}` or `RoleWindowMenu` their standard items. On macOS an `Accelerator` is the key equivalent (the key does not reach the app): write `CmdOrCtrl+N`.
- **Settings v2:** `contrast-more:` is the variant for the system's high contrast (`tela.UseHighContrast()` in code). The system's text scale works like a browser's default font size: 1rem is the theme's rem times the scale, so `text-*` and rem spacing (`p-4`, `gap-2`, `w-64`, breakpoints) grow together while px values (`border`, `text-[13px]`, `w-[320px]`) do not; `tela.UseTextScale()` returns it for sizes computed in code, and `tela.App{IgnoreTextScale: true}` opts a fixed layout out. `tela.UseAccentColor() (Color, bool)` is the system accent (false: none). In tests and snapshots the scale is 1 and the accent absent unless set.

```go
package integration

import (
	"errors"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
)

// DropZone takes files dropped from a file manager.
type DropZone struct{ OnFiles func([]string) }

func (d DropZone) Build() tela.Node {
	depth, setDepth := tela.UseState(0) // enters minus leaves
	files := func(dt *tela.DataTransfer) bool { return dt.Has("Files") }
	border, label := "border-border contrast-more:border-foreground", "Drop files here"
	if depth > 0 {
		border, label = "border-primary bg-primary/5", "Release to add them"
	}
	return Div(Class("rounded-lg border-2 border-dashed p-8 text-center", border), TestID("drop"),
		OnDragEnter(func(e tela.DragEvent) {
			if files(e.DataTransfer) {
				setDepth.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 })
			}
		}),
		OnDragOver(func(e tela.DragEvent) {
			if files(e.DataTransfer) {
				e.PreventDefault() // accept: the drop comes here
			}
		}),
		OnDragLeave(func(e tela.DragEvent) {
			if files(e.DataTransfer) {
				setDepth.Update(func(n int) int { return max(n-1, 0) })
			}
		}),
		OnDrop(func(e tela.DragEvent) {
			setDepth.Set(0)
			d.OnFiles(e.DataTransfer.Files())
		}),
		Text(label))
}

// Card is dragged to a target of the app, or to another application as text.
type Card struct {
	ID, Title string
	OnMoved   func(id string)
}

func (c Card) Build() tela.Node {
	return Div(Draggable(true), TestID("card-"+c.ID), Class("cursor-grab rounded-md border p-3"),
		OnDragStart(func(e tela.DragEvent) {
			e.DataTransfer.SetData("application/x-card", c.ID)
			e.DataTransfer.SetText(c.Title)
			e.DataTransfer.EffectAllowed = tela.DropMove
		}),
		OnDragEnd(func(e tela.DragEvent) {
			if e.DataTransfer.DropEffect == tela.DropMove {
				c.OnMoved(c.ID) // a target took it
			}
		}),
		Text(c.Title))
}

// CopyTitle puts a title on the clipboard as text; Paste reads it back.
func CopyTitle(title string) error {
	var dt tela.DataTransfer
	dt.SetText(title)
	return desktop.WriteClipboard(&dt)
}

func Paste(done func(text string)) error {
	return desktop.ReadClipboard(func(dt *tela.DataTransfer, err error) {
		if err == nil {
			done(dt.Text())
		}
	})
}

// Quick makes a note from anywhere (a global shortcut) and from links and files (UseLaunch).
type Quick struct{}

func (Quick) Build() tela.Node {
	win := tela.UseWindow()
	notes, setNotes := tela.UseState([]string{})
	hint, setHint := tela.UseState("")
	add := func(s string) { setNotes.Update(func(n []string) []string { return append(n, s) }) }
	desktop.UseLaunch(func(l desktop.Launch) { // the start, then every forwarded start
		for _, u := range l.URLs() { // notes:new?text=hi
			add(u)
		}
		for _, p := range l.Files() {
			add(p)
		}
	})
	return Div(Class("p-4"),
		desktop.GlobalShortcut{
			ID: "quick-note", Keys: "Ctrl+Alt+N", Description: "Create a note",
			OnPress: func() { win.Show(); add("Untitled note") },
			OnStatus: func(e desktop.ShortcutStatusEvent) {
				if e.Status != desktop.ShortcutBound {
					setHint.Set(e.Err.Error()) // taken, refused, removed or unsupported
				}
			},
		},
		P(Textf("%d notes", len(notes))), P(Text(hint)))
}

// App is a single-instance app: a second start hands its launch to the first.
var App = desktop.SingleInstance(tela.App{AppID: "com.example.notes", Title: "Notes", Root: Quick{}})

// RegisterLinks makes the app a candidate for notes: links; the default only if the user asks.
// It does file or registry I/O: call it at start, off the UI thread.
func RegisterLinks(makeDefault bool) (desktop.Registration, error) {
	scheme := desktop.URLScheme("notes")
	if _, err := desktop.Register(scheme); err != nil {
		return desktop.Registration{}, err // errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrAssociationTaken): another app holds it
	}
	if makeDefault {
		if _, err := desktop.MakeDefault(scheme); err != nil {
			return desktop.Registration{}, err
		}
	}
	return desktop.RegistrationStatus(scheme)
}

// Vault unlocks a key kept in the OS's keyring. The secret calls block: use a goroutine.
type Vault struct{}

func (Vault) Build() tela.Node {
	state, setState := tela.UseState("locked")
	unlock := func() {
		go func() { // the keyring may be waiting for the user
			_, err := desktop.Secret("library-key")
			switch {
			case err == nil:
				setState.Set("unlocked")
			case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrSecretNotFound):
				setState.Set("no key yet")
			case errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrSecretCanceled):
				setState.Set("the keyring stayed locked")
			default: // desktop.ErrUnsupported: no keyring
				setState.Set("no keyring")
			}
		}()
	}
	return Div(Button(OnClick(unlock), Text("Unlock")), Text(state))
}
```

```go
package integration

import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"
)

// NoteMenu opens the OS's context menu where there is one, the drawn one elsewhere.
func NoteMenu(title string, onDelete func()) tela.Node {
	return kit.ContextMenu[string]{
		Native: kit.NativeOn, // NativeAuto (zero) follows tela.App{NativeMenus: true}
		Items: []kit.MenuItem[string]{
			{Key: "copy", Label: "Copy link", Shortcut: "Ctrl+L"},
			{Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
			{Key: "delete", Label: "Delete", Variant: kit.Destructive, OnSelect: onDelete},
		},
		Children: Div(Class("rounded-lg border p-4"), Text(title)),
	}
}

// Readout follows the system's contrast, text scale and accent color.
type Readout struct{}

func (Readout) Build() tela.Node {
	scale := tela.UseTextScale() // 1.25: 1rem is 20 px
	accent, ok := tela.UseAccentColor()
	if !ok {
		accent = tela.Hex("#4f46e5")
	}
	return Div(Class("rounded-lg border border-border p-4 text-sm contrast-more:border-2 contrast-more:border-foreground"),
		Style(tela.Bg(accent)), Textf("Text scale %.2f", scale))
}
```

## 9. Pitfalls and limits

| Mistake | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Div("Hello")` does not compile | `Div(Text("Hello"))`; formatted: `Textf("%d", n)` |
| Calling a function component that uses hooks: `counter()`, `telatest.Mount(t, counter())`, `Card{}.Build()` (dev mode panics: "hook called outside its component") | `tela.C(counter)` (write a public `Counter()` that returns it once), `tela.CP(fn, props)`, or pass the struct value itself: `Card{}` |
| A hook inside `if`, a loop, a `Map`/`VirtualList` callback, an event handler, or after an early `return` | Call every hook at the top of the component; move per-row state into a row component (`MapKeyed(items, key, func(T) tela.Component { return Row{...} })`) |
| Returning a prop where a node is expected: `return Class("p-4")`, or a `Map` callback that returns `Key(x.ID)` (it compiles, because a prop has a `Build` method, and panics in dev mode; `tela lint` reports `prop-node`) | Props go to an element: `Div(Class("p-4"), ...)`, `Div(Key(x.ID), ...)` |
| `Fragment(kit.Button{...})`, `Fragment(x)` around a single node, or `tela.Node{}` / `n.IsZero()` for the empty node (removed) | `kit.Button{...}`, `x`, `nil` / `n == nil`; `tela lint -fix` removes the single-child `Fragment`s |
| A list from `Map` without keys (dev warning "list without keys"), or index keys on a list that reorders | `Key(item.ID)` on each element; `tela.WithKey(comp, id)` for components; `MapKeyed` |
| Declaring a name that `h` exports in your package (`Button`, `Label`, `Input`, `Text`, `Icon`, `Form`, `Value`, `Name`, `Type`, `Key`, `Map`, `Range`, `Scale`, `Style`, `Rows`, `ID`, `P`, `A`, `Code`...): "already declared through dot-import" | Name it `SaveButton`, `FieldLabel`, `themes`... |
| `&Card{}` as a child, or a prop in a `tela.Component` field (`Children: Class("p-4")`): dev panic | Pass `Card{}`; put props in `Class`/`Props` |
| `setCount.Set(count + 1)` twice in one frame loses one | `setCount.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 })`; `tela.Toggle(setOpen)` for bools |
| `UseEffect(f, nil)` (dev panic) | `tela.UseEffect(f, tela.Once)` or `tela.UseMount(f)` |
| Unknown or misspelled class (`rounded-xxl`, `bg-primry`) | Dev error with "did you mean"; `tela lint ./...` finds them statically. Unsupported classes say what to use |
| A `kit.Tooltip` and a `kit.DropdownMenu` on the same `kit.Button`: a trigger takes one overlay | Tooltip on a wrapper: `kit.Tooltip{Content: Text("More"), Trigger: kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node { return Span(p, Class("flex"), kit.DropdownMenu[string]{...}) })}` |
| A trigger that is not a `kit.Button` (an `h.Button`, an avatar) | `kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node { return Button(p, ...) })`: put `p` on the element. `Disabled` goes on the overlay |
| `kit.Field` around `h.Input`, around two controls, or around an overlay trigger (`AlertDialog`, `Dialog`, `Popover`): the label names nothing or the wrong one | One kit control per `Field` (`kit.Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `DatePicker`, `ColorInput`); a label + button row is a `Div` (`SignOutRow` above); `RadioGroup`/`ToggleGroup` go in a `kit.FieldSet` (legend names them) or take `AriaLabel`; `Slider` and `Progress` take `AriaLabel` |
| An absolutely positioned icon over an input swallows clicks | `pointer-events-none` on the decoration: `Icon(lucide.Search, Class("pointer-events-none absolute top-2.5 left-3 size-4 text-muted-foreground"))` with `kit.Input{Class: "pl-9"}` |
| Scrolling to the newest item flickers or lands short | `UseLayoutEffect` + `ref.ScrollIntoView()` (or `ScrollToIndex(i, tela.AlignEnd)` on a `VirtualList`), deps = the item count |
| A flex child does not scroll or overflows | Give the scroll container a definite height (`h-screen`, `flex-1 min-h-0` in a `flex-col`, `h-96`) and `overflow-y-auto`; `min-w-0` on flex children that hold truncated text |
| Wanting `kit.Alert`, `kit.Sheet`, `kit.Accordion`, `kit.Breadcrumb`, `kit.Sidebar`, `kit.Combobox` | Not in kit: compose `Div`s with tokens (`Role("alert")` for an alert, a `Div` sidebar with `AriaCurrent`), or use `kit.Dialog`/`kit.Popover`; `aria` has `UseCombobox` for a hand-built one |
| `Variant: "primary"` on a `kit.Button` | The default variant is the zero value; variants are `Secondary`, `Outline`, `Ghost`, `Destructive`, `Link` |
| `tela snapshot --dark` still renders light (or the other way round), or every render has one scheme | `App.ColorScheme` is set to `tela.Light`/`tela.Dark` and overrides the flag: leave it `tela.System` |
| A kit page that looks off (square corners, wrong colors) | `Theme: &theme` with `theme := kit.Theme()` and `RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground"` on the `App` |
| Palette colors that ignore dark mode (`bg-white`, `text-zinc-900`) | Tokens (`bg-card`, `text-foreground`), or add `dark:` pairs |
| The snapshot does not show a toast or effect result | `tela snapshot` renders one frame; in `tela mcp`, act then `wait {"ms": 300}` and `screenshot` |
| `h.A` link does nothing | Tela does not navigate: handle `OnClick` |
| `Div(Class("flex"), children...)` with a `[]tela.Node` slice: Go cannot spread it | `Div(Class("flex"), Nodes(children))` |
| A `tela.Window` without `OnClose`: its close button does nothing | `OnClose: func() { setOpen.Set(false) }`: state owns whether a window exists |
| `desktop.OpenFile`, `ShowMessage` or `Notify` from a goroutine (dev panic), or state set in the callback of a goroutine | Call them from handlers and effects, or inside `tela.Post(func() { ... })`; their callbacks run on the UI thread |
| `App.OnClose` hides the window but nothing can show it again (no tray, or the tray is unsupported) | Pair it with a `desktop.Tray` whose `OnError` turns the hiding off; `tela.Quit` from the menu |
| `kit.TitleBar` in a window that keeps the OS's title bar: two bars | `Frameless: true`, or draw it only when `tela.UseWindow().State().ClientSideDecorations` |
| A test reads or writes the real settings and window placements | `telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t)` at its start |
| A drop zone never gets `OnDrop`, or flickers while the drag moves over its children | Call `e.PreventDefault()` in `OnDragOver`; count enters and leaves (the new element's enter comes before the old one's leave) instead of a bool |
| `desktop.Secret`/`SetSecret` in a handler, an effect or a build (dev warning; the keyring may wait for the user, so the app freezes) | A goroutine (`go func() {...}()` or `tela.UseGo`) that sets state with a `Setter`; handle `ErrSecretCanceled` and `ErrUnsupported` |
| `desktop.Register` for a link or file type, then expecting it to be the default or to replace another app's | It makes the app a candidate only. `MakeDefault` on the user's request; `Replace()` only after asking; under `go run`/`tela dev` give `ForApp(HandlerApp{Exec: ...})` |
| A `GlobalShortcut` that "does nothing" | Show `OnStatus`: it may be taken, refused by the user, or unsupported; a nil `OnStatus` only warns in dev mode |

**Limits.** Linux (Wayland, X11), Windows and macOS 13+ windows; on macOS, window control and the desktop services (dialogs, tray, notifications, menus, drag and drop) are not there yet. Wayland cannot place windows or keep them on top, and Windows notifications have no action buttons; a tray needs a host on Linux (GNOME needs an extension). No submenus in menus; `Checkbox` has no indeterminate state; `Select` has no search (build a combobox with `aria.UseCombobox`); `Table` is virtual only with a fixed `RowHeight`, and has no column resizing or row selection UI; no date-time input; no `tela add` yet. No margin collapsing, floats or CSS tables; 2D transforms only; SVG icons have no text, filters or patterns; no `grid-template-areas` from classes; `vertical-align` only on inline-blocks.

## 10. Testing

`telatest` mounts a component in a headless window, drives it with real events, finds elements like Playwright and compares goldens (`testdata/<name>.png`; `TELA_UPDATE=1 go test ./...` writes them). Dev errors fail the test.

```go
func TestSettingsLike(t *testing.T) {
	app := telatest.MountFunc(t, func() tela.Node {
		on, setOn := tela.UseState(false)
		return Div(Class("p-6"),
			kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Label: "Weekly digest",
				Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &on, OnCheckedChange: setOn.Set}},
			If(on, P(Text("Subscribed"))))
	}, telatest.Size(480, 200), telatest.Theme(kit.Theme()))

	digest := telatest.ByRole("switch", "Weekly digest")
	app.Expect(digest, telatest.Checked(false))
	app.Click(digest) // also: Fill(loc, text), Press("Shift+Tab"), Press("ControlOrMeta+s") (Meta under telatest.PlatformKeys("darwin")), Hover, Click(loc, telatest.Right()), Tap, LongPress
	app.Expect(digest, telatest.Checked(true), telatest.Disabled(false))
	app.ExpectText("Subscribed")
	app.Advance(500 * time.Millisecond) // the clock is manual: timers, UseTimeout, animations
	app.Golden("digest_on.png")         // telatest.Dark(), telatest.Scale(2) for other renders
}
```

`telatest.Mount(t, comp, opts...)` mounts any component (`Settings()`, `Page{}`, `Previews["x"]`); `telatest.MountApp(t, App, opts...)` mounts a `tela.App` as its window would. Locators: `ByRole(role, name)`, `ByText(text)`, `ByTestID(id)`, `ByClass(...)`, then `.Nth(i)`, `.Filter(telatest.HasText("x"))`. Expectations wait and retry: `Expect(loc, Checked/Pressed/Selected/Expanded/Disabled/Focused/Invalid(bool), Current("page"), HasName, HasValue)`, `ExpectText`, `ExpectNoText`, `ExpectRole`, `ExpectCount`, `ExpectValue`, `ExpectAria(yaml)`. `AriaSnapshot()`, `Screenshot()`, `Bounds(loc)`, `Resize(w, h)` inspect without waiting. Several windows: `app.Windows()`, `app.Window("Settings")` and `app.WaitForWindow(func() { app.Click(open) })` give an `*App` scoped to that window, with the whole API above; also `RequestClose()` (the close button), `Maximize()`, `Minimize()`, `ExpectWindowState(telatest.Maximized(true))` (`Fullscreen`, `Minimized`, `Hidden`, `Active`, `ClientDecorations`), `ExpectTitle`, `ExpectWindowCount(n)`, `ExpectClosed()`, `ExpectQuit()` and `ExpectRunning()` (an `OnClose` that hides the window). `MountApp` applies the window fields of the `tela.App` (`Frameless`, `OnClose`, size limits...); for a custom title bar, `HitRegions()`, `HitAt(x, y)` and `CaptionDrags()` show what the OS would do.

**Desktop services in tests.** The headless desktop shows nothing: it records dialogs, notifications and tray icons, and the test answers them, as the user would. Call `telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t)` first in a test whose app uses `desktop.UseSetting`, `PersistApp` or the app folders, or it reads and writes the real ones. Nothing answers by itself.

```go
package notes

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/telatest"
)

func TestEditorServices(t *testing.T) {
	telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t) // settings and window placements go to a temporary folder
	app := telatest.Mount(t, Editor())

	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open…"))
	app.AnswerFileDialog("/home/ana/ideas.md") // no paths: the user cancels
	app.ExpectText("/home/ana/ideas.md")

	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Close"))
	app.AnswerMessage(desktop.AnswerYes) // native or drawn box: the same call
	app.ExpectWindowState(telatest.Hidden(true))
	app.ExpectRunning()

	app.ClickTrayItem("Show Notes") // also ClickTray(), Tray(), Trays()
	app.ExpectWindowState(telatest.Hidden(false))

	app.Unsupported(telatest.FileDialogs) // from now on OpenFile returns ErrUnsupported
	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open…"))
	app.ExpectRole("textbox", "") // the fallback path field
}
```

Also `app.Notifications()`, `ClickNotification(title)`, `ClickNotificationAction(title, label)`, `DismissNotification(title)` and `MessageBoxes()` / `FileDialogs()` to check what was asked. `Unsupported` takes `telatest.FileDialogs`, `MessageBoxes` (the box is drawn then), `Notifications`, `TrayIcons` and `OpenURLs`; with no arguments everything is supported again.

**Integration services in tests.** The headless desktop plays the OS for each feature, and nothing touches the real clipboard, keyring, registry, shortcuts or menus. Call `telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t)` first.

- **Drag and drop:** `app.DropFiles(loc, paths...)` and `app.DropData(loc, payload)` (payloads `telatest.DragFiles`, `DragText`, `DragHTML`, `DragPNG`, `DragType(mime, s)`, combined with `.And`) drop what another application drags and return the `tela.DropEffect` the app accepted (`tela.DropNone`: refused). Steps: `app.HoverDrag(loc, telatest.Carrying(p))` (the drag-over state), `app.LeaveDrag()`, `app.CancelDrag()`, `app.DropOn(loc)`. A drag of your own `Draggable`: `app.DragTo(from, to)` (also `DragToWindow(from, otherWindow, to)`), or `app.StartDrag(from)` then `DropOutside(tela.DropMove)` for a drop in another application.
- **Shortcuts and launches:** `app.GlobalShortcuts()` (what is registered), `app.PressShortcut(id)`, `ReleaseShortcut(id)`, `app.SetShortcutStatus(id, desktop.ShortcutTaken, "")` (also `ShortcutRefused`, `ShortcutRevoked`, `ShortcutBound` with a trigger), `app.SetShortcutUnassigned(id)`, `app.FailShortcuts(err)`; `app.InjectLaunch(desktop.Launch{Args: ...})` plays a second start. `desktop.SingleInstance` claims nothing in tests.
- **Clipboard, secrets, registration:** `app.Clipboard()` / `app.SetClipboard(&dt)`; `app.StoredSecret(name)`, `app.SetStoredSecret(name, b)`, `app.FailSecrets(desktop.ErrSecretCanceled)` (`nil` stops failing); `app.Registrations()`, `app.HoldAssociation(assoc, "Other App")` (another app owns it), `app.SetDefaultHandler(assoc, "Other App")`, `app.RegisteredApps()`. `app.Trashed()` (the paths `desktop.MoveToTrash` moved; the headless trash moves them into a temporary folder), `app.FailTrash(err)`. `app.Unsupported(telatest.Secrets)` (also `GlobalShortcuts`, `NativeMenus`, `ClipboardData`, `Associations`, `Trash`) tests the fallbacks.
- **Menus and settings:** `telatest.PreferNativeMenus()` is `App.NativeMenus`; `app.PopupMenus()`, `app.ChoosePopupItem(path...)`, `app.DismissPopupMenu()` answer a native context menu, `app.MenuBar()` and `app.ChooseMenuItem("File", "New")` a native menu bar, `app.AppMenuBar()`, `AppMenuItems()` and `ChooseAppMenuItem("File", "New")` the app's (`WithUnsupported(telatest.AppMenu)` plays Windows). `app.RequestQuit()` plays Cmd+Q; options `TitleBarOverlay()` and `TitleBarControls(rect)` (`PlatformKeys("darwin")` gives the Mac's). The options `telatest.HighContrast()`, `TextScale(1.25)`, `AccentColor(c)` set the system's settings at mount; `app.SetDarkMode(bool)`, `SetHighContrast`, `SetTextScale`, `SetAccentColor`, `SetReducedMotion` change them while it runs.

```go
package integration

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/telatest"
)

func TestDropAndShortcut(t *testing.T) {
	telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t)
	var dropped []string
	zone := telatest.Mount(t, DropZone{OnFiles: func(f []string) { dropped = f }})
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ideas.md")
	zone.HoverDrag(telatest.ByTestID("drop"), telatest.Carrying(telatest.DragFiles(path)))
	zone.ExpectText("Release to add them") // the drag-over state
	if zone.DropOn(telatest.ByTestID("drop")) == tela.DropNone || len(dropped) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the drop was refused: %v", dropped)
	}

	app := telatest.MountApp(t, App)
	app.PressShortcut("quick-note")
	app.ExpectText("1 notes")
	app.InjectLaunch(desktop.Launch{Args: []string{"notes:open?id=3"}})
	app.ExpectText("2 notes")
	app.SetShortcutStatus("quick-note", desktop.ShortcutTaken, "")
	app.ExpectText("taken by another application")
}

func TestVaultAndLinks(t *testing.T) {
	telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t)
	app := telatest.Mount(t, Vault{})
	app.FailSecrets(desktop.ErrSecretCanceled) // the user dismissed the unlock prompt
	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Unlock"))
	app.ExpectText("the keyring stayed locked")
	app.FailSecrets(nil)
	app.SetStoredSecret("library-key", []byte("k"))
	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Unlock"))
	app.ExpectText("unlocked")

	app.HoldAssociation(desktop.URLScheme("notes"), "Other App")
	if _, err := RegisterLinks(false); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("registered over another application")
	}
	app.HoldAssociation(desktop.URLScheme("notes"), "")
	app.SetDefaultHandler(desktop.URLScheme("notes"), "Other App") // the user's default
	if reg, err := RegisterLinks(false); err != nil || !reg.Registered || reg.Default {
		t.Fatalf("a candidate, not the default: %+v, %v", reg, err)
	}
}

func TestNativeMenuAndSettings(t *testing.T) {
	app := telatest.Mount(t, NoteMenu("Groceries", func() {}), telatest.Size(300, 200))
	app.Click(telatest.ByText("Groceries"), telatest.Right())
	app.ChoosePopupItem("Delete")

	ro := telatest.Mount(t, Readout{}, telatest.TextScale(1.5), telatest.HighContrast())
	ro.ExpectText("Text scale 1.50")
	ro.SetTextScale(2)
	ro.ExpectText("Text scale 2.00")
}
```
